context: Row 1361 (all previous fixes active): A 35.5s with 2 slices (was 55.5s), B+C still 89.0s, total AI 124.5s, cost $0.136, ~42.5k output tokens. B+C confirms the throughput ceiling on the API key. Next lever chosen by the user: cut the tokens of the extraction stage.
feature: Idea 2 — the raw analyte line is rebuilt in C# instead of being retyped by the model
why: KeyResult.AnalyteLineRaw is a VERBATIM copy of a report line that the app already holds in memory in TEXT mode. Making the model re-emit 84 full lines was roughly 30-40% of the extraction stage's generated tokens, for a result a string search produces in microseconds.
implementation: Services/RawLineReconstructor.cs — for every analyte with an EMPTY raw line, finds the report line containing the normalized parameter name, scoring candidates so the actual result row wins over a comment that merely mentions the analyte (value present +4, line not yet used +2). Diacritics, spacing and separators are normalized, so 'Colesterol total' matches 'COLESTEROL  TOTAL' and comma decimals match.
Wired in InterpretationController right after the lab-marker sanitizer and BEFORE the LOINC matcher, which uses that line as context. Works for BOTH pipelines.
Stage A's contract now asks the model to skip analyte_line_raw — but ONLY in TEXT mode. In VISION mode (scanned PDFs) there is no text to rebuild from, so the model keeps emitting it.
Purely additive: a raw line already produced by the model is never overwritten.
expected_effect: Extraction stage output down ~30-40% (13.5k -> ~8.5k tokens), so A ~35.5s -> ~22-25s and a lower A cost. NOT yet measured against the real API.
